input: Is Elden Ring harder than Dark Souls III?
output: Elden Ring is comparably challenging but approaches difficulty differently. While Dark Souls III has tighter, more linear level design, Elden Ring's open world lets you tackle bosses in various orders and level up more freely, which can actually make it feel slightly more forgiving if you explore thoroughly. That said, late-game bosses in Elden Ring are notoriously punishing, so difficulty is subjective based on your approach.

output: Most players spend around 80 hours to complete the main story and explore significantly, though this varies wildly depending on your playstyle. Completionists hunting every item, NPC questline, and optional boss could easily hit 120+ hours, while speedrunners or those using guides might finish in 40-50 hours. input: Should I play Elden Ring if I've never played a Souls-like game?
output: Elden Ring is actually one of the best entry points into Souls-likes because of its open world—you can explore at your own pace, level up in easier areas, and come back to tough bosses later when you're stronger. However, you should go in prepared for a very challenging experience where patience, learning enemy patterns, and accepting deaths are part of the journey. If you enjoy deep lore, build experimentation, and the satisfaction of finally defeating a boss that's destroyed you 20 times, it's absolutely worth trying.
